sections.title: Building bigger numbers
sections.content: 11–19 are built with *tizen-* ('teen') plus the digit you already know: *tizen* + *egy* = *tizenegy* (11), *tizen* + *öt* = *tizenöt* (15). The tens each get their own word — *húsz* (20), *harminc* (30), *negyven* (40), *ötven* (50), *hatvan* (60), *hetven* (70), *nyolcvan* (80), *kilencven* (90), *száz* (100) — and everything in between is just ten-word + digit stuck together, no space: *harminckettő* (32), *kilencvenhét* (97). The one exception is the 20s, which use *huszon-* instead of *húsz-*: *huszonegy* (21), not *húszegy*.

The one irregular spot is the 20s: they use *huszon-*, not *húsz-*, so *huszonegy* (21), *huszonkettő* (22) — not *húszegy*, *húszkettő*. Every other decade just glues the tens word straight onto the digit with no change and no space, e.g. *negyvenhat* (46), *hetvenhárom* (73).
